links.outcome: Abstention/deferral rate and accuracy before vs after RLVR/GRPO training on MedQA-USMLE
links.effect: Abstention rate rose from 3.5% to 8.0% (+129%), while raw accuracy fell from 44.0% to 35.5% (an 'Alignment Tax').
links.quote: Our results show a clear 'Alignment Tax' on raw accuracy (decreasing from 44.0% to 35.5% on MedQA-USMLE).

unlisted_practices: Training small language models with RLVR and GRPO to embed calibrated abstention and clinical deferral behavior

screen.reason: The paper investigates a model training/fine-tuning methodology (RLVR with GRPO) to embed abstention/deferral behavior into a small language model evaluated on the MedQA-USMLE benchmark, rather than testing a health care deployment practice or organizational guardrail applied to an existing tool.
